note: 目标 encaustic-painting 全正文全部FAQ核读。原句：Encaustic painting's origin is uncertain by its own earliest chronicler: writing around 77 AD, Pliny the Elder stated flatly that \"it is not agreed who was the inventor of painting in wax,\" recording several competing claims before crediting Pausias of Sicyon as the first artist to become famous at it. The \"Punic wax\" recipe long cited as the medium behind the Fayum mummy portraits fares no better under modern testing: a 2020 study published by Getty, focused on two Art Institute of Chicago portraits, reviewed recipes recorded from Otto Donner von Richter in 1893 through Euphrosyne Doxiadis in the 1990s, and repeated as settled fact in reference works including The Oxford History of Western Art, and reported that scientific analysis had not established those specific combinations in mummy portraits. Identifying beeswax does not establish how it was prepared. The same study found beeswax as the major binder in both paintings, including one that looks nothing like encaustic, undercutting the visual test art historians have used for over a century to sort portraits into \"encaustic\" and \"tempera\" groups.。源当前句：A similar gap between an assumed technique and what the documented record actually supports shows up in [the proposed Punic-wax formulas for Fayum portraits, whose preparation cannot be established simply by identifying beeswax](/encaustic-painting/).。本批全读原及改稿5FAQ，Getty2020完整相关主文证实分析出beeswax并不定制备recipe。原never found概括过强，改为recipe preparation无法仅由binder识别；两knownglazes与ancient uncertainty明确分开。

目标 cloisonne 全正文全部FAQ核读。原句：Cloisonné's reputation as an old, unbroken craft doesn't match the documented record in any of the three traditions most associated with it. In China, the earliest written mention of the technique is dismissive: Cao Zhao's 1388 antiquities guide, the Gegu Yaolun, rules copper enamelware fit only for a woman's chamber and, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art's account of that judgment, \"not well suited to a more restrained atmosphere, such as that of a scholar's home.\" Within about 40 years, by the Ming Xuande reign (1426-35), the same technique had become prized ware at the imperial court, the period from which the earliest securely dated Chinese cloisonné survives. Byzantium had no comparable gap: the Met holds a gold and cloisonné-enamel reliquary made in the early ninth century to hold a fragment of the True Cross, and Venice's Basilica di San Marco has displayed a gold altarpiece carrying more than eighty Byzantine cloisonné enamels since 976. Japan's version shows two real breaks instead, and Sotheby's historical account states plainly that no three-dimensional cloisonné was produced there again until a former samurai, Kaji Tsunekichi, took apart an imported enamel piece in the late 1830s.。源当前句：Reputation can swing the opposite way just as fast: [the antiquarian Cao Zhao dismissed cloisonné enamel as unfit for a scholar's studio in 1388, only for the same technique to become an imperial treasure within about forty years](/cloisonne/), a reminder that a decorative craft's status, like its name, is rarely as stable as the finished object makes it look.。全读1388CaoZhao/1426–35Xuande起已securecourtobjects及全FAQ。约40年范围支持声誉变迁，已撤leading排名；不把该短时间变迁当所有cloisonne不连续证据，其他已发现目标事实债务排额外批。
